options: All the use cases and requirements outlined in the Functional Requirements Document (FRD) or business requirement specifications, ensuring the product operates as intended
The speed of the system under peak load
The security of the system against SQL injection
The ease of use of the interface
The cost of running the system in production
questions.explanation: Functional testing validates the use cases and requirements in the FRD or other business requirement specifications to ensure the product operates as intended.

questions.stem: How is the focus of functional testing distinguished from that of non-functional testing?
options: Functional testing focuses on cost; non-functional testing focuses on features
Functional testing focuses on what the system does; non-functional testing focuses on how the system performs
Functional testing is automated; non-functional testing is always manual
Functional testing is done by users; non-functional testing is done by developers
Functional testing focuses on security; non-functional testing focuses on correctness
questions.explanation: Functional testing is concerned with what the system does, while non-functional testing evaluates how the system performs and behaves.

questions.stem: Why is functional testing described as a black box testing technique?
options: Because the results are hidden from stakeholders
Because it is run in a darkened room
Because it does not require knowledge of the internal code or architecture
Because it only tests error messages
Because it requires reading the source code line by line
questions.explanation: Functional testing is black box because it does not require knowledge of the internal code or architecture; it focuses on user requirements and use cases.

questions.stem: Testing the integration between a payment gateway and an e-commerce platform is an example of which type of functional testing?
questions.explanation: Integration testing verifies the interaction between integrated modules or systems, such as a payment gateway and an e-commerce platform.

questions.stem: Which type of functional testing validates the software against user requirements and business goals and often involves stakeholders or end-users?
questions.explanation: Acceptance testing validates the software against user requirements and business goals, often involving stakeholders or end-users before deployment.

questions.stem: Which type of non-functional testing tests the system under extreme conditions to identify its breaking points?
questions.explanation: Stress testing pushes the system under extreme conditions, such as overloading a server with requests, to observe when it fails.

questions.stem: Running a banking application continuously for 48 hours to check for failures is an example of which non-functional test?
questions.explanation: Reliability testing assesses the software's consistency over time under specific conditions, such as continuous operation for 48 hours.

questions.stem: Which tools are listed for non-functional testing rather than functional testing?
questions.explanation: JMeter, LoadRunner and OWASP ZAP are non-functional testing tools; Selenium, QTP and Test Complete are listed for functional testing.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a step in the process of functional testing?
options: Define quality attributes such as performance benchmarks
questions.explanation: Defining quality attributes such as performance benchmarks is the first step of the non-functional testing process, not the functional one.

questions.stem: Which of the following is listed as a challenge in functional and non-functional testing?
options: Tools being too easy to use
Ambiguous requirements that hinder test planning
questions.explanation: Challenges include ambiguous requirements, resource limitations, complex systems and the difficulty of simulating real-world scenarios.
